dimensions.assessment: Affects trademark and copyright owners, CBP officers, online marketplaces, freight forwarders, and parties with an interest in imported merchandise.
dimensions.evidence: any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner.

dimensions.assessment: Modifies evidentiary standards ('reasonable suspicion') and expands the scope of nonpublic data and packing information shareable during investigations.
dimensions.evidence: striking 'suspects' and inserting 'has a reasonable suspicion'

dimensions.assessment: Contains no federal spending authorizations, revenue changes, or economic appropriations.
Amends Section 628A of the Tariff Act of 1930 to alter agency information-sharing regulations and allowable parties.
dimensions.evidence: Section 628A of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1628a) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Makes permanent statutory changes to federal customs trade enforcement procedures.

missing_information: Specific regulatory definitions for Secretary-prescribed notification rules are omitted.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill expands Customs and Border Protection information-sharing authorities regarding suspected intellectual property violations in international trade.
